screens.title: Plant list

conventions.browser_back: One page with no in-page history: nothing is pushed on the history stack, so Back leaves Waterlog to the previous page, and Forward returns to a freshly loaded list.
conventions.keyboard_path: Tab order: Skip to the plants, then each plant's Watered button in list order (Try again in the unreachable state). Enter or Space activates. Focus stays on a row's button while it logs and after it succeeds; a failure's message is announced (role=alert) and focus stays on the button so it can be retried. A success shows 'Logged a watering for <name>.' in a polite live region above the list.
conventions.hover: Buttons brighten slightly on hover; nothing is revealed on hover only.
conventions.context_menu: The browser's own; Waterlog adds none.

screens.notes: Layouts: 360 stacks each row (name with its Due label, interval, last watering, then a full-width Watered button at least 48 px tall); 720 puts the button, at least 160 px wide, at the row's right; 1280 lays each row out as columns name | interval | last watering | button in a 960 px column. Last watering shows as a local date and time, or 'Never watered'. Due is the text label 'Due' (bold, outlined amber pill with a drop glyph) plus a thick amber left edge and an amber-tinted card, never colour alone. A row just watered shows the text 'Watered just now' with a check, in the done colours. Text is at least 16 px (body 18 px), and interval and last watering carry their values in bold. list_plants errors (405, 500) and an unreachable service all show 'Can't reach Waterlog.' with Try again; every log_watering error (400, 404, 405, 500) keeps the row as it was and shows 'Couldn't log the watering. Try again.' under it. The header uses the logo slot's on_dark variant on header_bg, the same in both themes. State markers: the screen's root carries data-state (web) or testID (android) set to one of state-loading, state-ok, state-empty, state-unreachable; each plant row carries data-row-state (web) or testID suffix (android) idle, watering, failed or watered. The web module draws it in public/index.html (the one page that draws every state of this screen), styled from public/tokens.css (the CSS binding of tokens.json).

screens.title: Plant list

conventions.back: The root and only screen: system Back (button or edge gesture) leaves the app as Android does by default; Waterlog intercepts nothing.

permissions.when: install time, granted by the system without asking; the app makes no runtime request and shows no prompt
permissions.denied: if the network is unavailable to the app, the list shows 'Can't reach Waterlog.' with Try again, as for an unreachable service

conventions.gestures: Taps only: Watered on a row, Try again on the unreachable state. No swipe, long-press or pull-to-refresh; touch targets are at least 48 dp.

screens.notes: Same workflow, wording and states as the web screen. Portrait lists one card per row, each with a full-width Watered button at least 48 dp tall under the plant's details, in thumb reach; landscape lists cards in two columns, in the API's order read row by row. A successful watering shows the confirmation 'Logged a watering for <name>.' at the top of the list, as on the web, and the row shows 'Watered just now'. The app bar shows the logo slot's on_dark variant on header_bg. Drawn as simulated_html mockups only; android/simulation/index.html draws the List (a due and a watered plant), Empty and Unreachable states from these. State markers: the screen's root carries data-state (web) or testID (android) set to one of state-loading, state-ok, state-empty, state-unreachable; each plant row carries data-row-state (web) or testID suffix (android) idle, watering, failed or watered. Due is the text label 'Due' (bold, outlined amber pill with a drop glyph) plus a thick amber left edge and an amber-tinted card, never colour alone. Text is at least 16 dp (body 18 dp). The android module builds every request of this screen on the one base URL in android/src/config.js, and android/simulation/index.html is the labelled preview of this screen's List, Empty and Unreachable states.
